simple.meaning: סְלִיחָה (çᵉlîychâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “pardon.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סְלִיחָה (H5547) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Nehemiah 9:17, with occurrences in Nehemiah, Psalms, Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סְלִיחָה (H5547) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in סְלִיחָה (H5547) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: סְלִיחָה (çᵉlîychâh) / H5547 is traced through Nehemiah 9:17, Psalms 130:4, Daniel 9:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: and refused to obey. They weren’t mindful of your wonders that you did among them, but hardened their neck, and in their rebellion appointed a captain to return to their bondage. But you are a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and didn’t forsake them.

timeline.evidenceText: and refused to obey.
